title: Now Daylight Floods the Morning Sky
description: Now Daylight Floods the Morning Sky in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Latin hymns of the early Church for Hymns of the Early Church (London, 1896), headed “Monday Morning”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now day-light floods the morn-ing sky, And earth-ward glides th'ap-proach-ing day, The danc-ing rays of sun-light chase The ga-thered fears of night a-way.

lines: Now daylight floods the morning sky,
And earthward glides the approaching day,
The dancing rays of sunlight chase
The gathered fears of night away.
Hence dreams that cloud the soul! away,
Ye terrors grim of midnight born!
Whate’er the dark of night hath bred,
Die in the light that greets the morn!
So when the day eternal breaks,—
That day for which our spirits long,—
Its light may fall to bless our souls,
E’en while we raise our morning song.
To God the Father throned in heaven,
To Christ the one begotten Son,
And to the Holy Ghost be praise,
Now, and while endless ages run.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Early Church (1896)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Latin, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Early Church; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
